## The Current Tariff Structure

As of 2026, most passenger vehicles and auto parts entering the US are subject to a 25% Section 232 tariff, applied on national security grounds. This rate applies broadly — to major exporting countries like Germany, Japan, and South Korea — unless the goods qualify for a specific exemption. [...] A declining offset for US-assembled vehicles.Automakers assembling vehicles in the US can apply for a partial offset against tariffs paid on imported parts, based on a percentage of the vehicle’s MSRP. This offset was set at 3.75% through April 2026 and has since stepped down to 2.5%, with a full phase-out planned by mid-2027 — a sign that the program is designed as a temporary transition tool rather than a permanent subsidy. In 2026, most US auto parts carry a 25% Section 232 tariff, while USMCA-qualifying parts stay duty-free. Stacking rules were removed, offsets are shrinking, and legal challenges continue. Importers should verify USMCA eligibility, tighten documentation, and build tariffs into pricing now.
